task_instance: Write user-facing UI copy (page title, buttons, empty state, loading state, error messages, confirmation dialog, tooltip, success toast) for a small 'Project Alerts' settings feature, following Sentry's brand guidelines (Plain Speech vs Sentry Voice tone selection, punctuation rules, American English spelling, word-choice avoid-list, button/error/empty-state/confirmation-dialog patterns, and anti-patterns), then programmatically verify the copy against those rules.
evidence: Created copy.json (13 UI copy items for a 'Project Alerts' feature) applying the skill's rules directly: tone selection (Plain Speech for buttons/errors/tooltips/settings, Sentry Voice for the empty state and loading state), no exclamation marks, no periods on short button labels, active voice, specific error messages (what happened + how to fix), specific confirmation dialog button/body text, avoidance of banned words ('Please', 'Sorry', 'Invalid', 'Success!', 'Oops') and anti-patterns ('has been successfully...', 'in order to'), American English spelling, and ALL CAPS reserved for acronyms only. Wrote verify.py, a rule-based checker that parses copy.json and flags: exclamation marks, disallowed ALL CAPS, British spellings, banned avoid-words, robot-speak anti-patterns, oversized/period-ending button text, and Sentry Voice misuse in error contexts. First run (`python3 verify.py`) caught a real violation: empty_state_action button text 'Create your first alert' exceeded the 3-word button-length guideline. Fixed it to 'Create Alert' and reran; final run exited 0 with 'All copy items pass brand-guidelines checks (tone, punctuation, spelling, word choice, anti-patterns).' Deliverable and verification live at copy.json and verify.py in the work directory; the whole task used only python3 and the local filesystem, no network or credentials needed.
